newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkism PM says targeting a balanced 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Turkism PM says targeting a balanced 1997 budget.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday the government was targeting a balanced budget in 1997.
"For the first time after many years, we targeted a balanced 1997 budget," Erbakan told reporters before meeting with senior officials to begin preparations of the 1997 budget.
Erbakan said according to the constitution, the new budget should be presented to the parliament by October 17.
"Our aim is to bring Turkey in a position to make investments and give services. We will consider all ongoing investments and give priority to the ones that have neared completion," he said.
The three-month-old government has unveiled two revenue-raising packages aimed to raise $10 billion each in the next three years to fight a huge fiscal deficit and hefty domestic borrowing.
Erbakan said new resource packages would follow the first two, adding that heavy domestic and foreign debt servicing crippled the budget.
"At the same time, we will try to bring domestic borrowing to an end," he told reporters.
Turkey's consolidated budget deficit jumped to 564 trillion lira in January-July this year from 103.3 trillion in the same 1995 period and 475.4 trillion in the first half of 1996.

Shortly after the government came to power in late June, Finance Minister Abdullatif Sener revised the deficit in the 3,511-trillion-lira 1996 budget to 1,300 trillion lira from an original target of 861 trillion.
Between 1,500 and 1,600 trillion lira is needed solely for domestic debt repayments this year.
